findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plaintext. User data is readable via the instance metadata service (including through SSRF) and is stored unencrypted in the AWS API and Terraform state, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true, routed to an internet gateway, and attached to a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22 and 80, making it directly reachable from the internet with no bastion or load balancer boundary.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so token-optional IMDSv1 is permitted. Combined with the plaintext credentials in user data and public reachability, this makes SSRF-based credential theft trivial.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance root volume may be created without EBS encryption at rest.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet on a publicly addressed host and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and only Apache over plain HTTP is provisioned in user data, so all web traffic to the instance is transmitted in cleartext.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host unrestricted outbound command-and-control and data-exfiltration channels.
The EBS volume is created with the encrypted attribute explicitly commented out, so data on the volume attached to the internet-facing web host is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption or KMS key is specified, so snapshot data is stored unencrypted and can be copied or shared without cryptographic protection.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry (valuable reconnaissance data) is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block and access controls
findings.description: No public access block, bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport, or object protection is configured for the security-log bucket, and force_destroy = true permits deletion of the logs, leaving it exposed to accidental public access, cleartext transport, and log tampering.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with a route table containing a 0.0.0.0/0 internet gateway route means every instance launched here is automatically internet-addressable, removing the network boundary in front of workloads.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the IGW-routed route table means any workload placed in this subnet is directly exposed to the internet.
